## Exploration

- {{< iconify fa6-solid book-open size=18px >}} Chapter One of
[Computer Systems Security: Planning for
Success](https://web.njit.edu/~rt494/security/)
- {{< iconify fa6-solid book-open size=18px >}} High-level references to
[Cracking Codes with Python](https://inventwithpython.com/cracking/)
- {{< iconify fa6-solid book-open size=18px >}} High-level references to [The Joy
of Cryptography](https://joyofcryptography.com/)
- {{< iconify fa6-solid book-open size=18px >}} High-level references to
[Operating Systems: Three Easy
Pieces](https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/OSTEP/)

## Activities

- {{< iconify fa6-solid people-line size=18px >}} **Monday and Wednesday**:
Course introduction
- {{< iconify fa6-solid people-line size=18px >}} **Friday**: Complete
programming skill check
- {{< iconify fa6-solid diagram-project size=18px >}} **Friday**: Continued
setup during laboratory session
  - Continued introduction to the computer security course
  - Continued highlighting of the concept of a "security synapse"
  - Introduction to basic computer security concepts and principles
  - If needed, continue to work on the programming skill check
  - In-person assessment in which students demonstrate the use of their
  installed software tools (e.g., download a Python script from the course web
  site and use `uv run` to execute it with an structure file input)
